name: mcp
description: Declarative MCP (Model Context Protocol) server: tools, resources and prompts backed by trusted project handlers

servers.description: MCP servers by name. Omitted (the scaffold default): nothing is mounted. Each needs a route <mount>/* with extension: mcp (POST, and HEAD).

mount.description: Exact endpoint path clients POST to; the route is <mount>/*, but the mount itself is the only path served (subpaths answer 404).

serverName.description: Server name reported in the initialize result (serverInfo.name).

serverVersion.description: Server version reported in the initialize result (serverInfo.version).

instructions.description: Optional usage instructions returned to clients in the initialize result.

title.description: Human-readable display name (the MCP title field); the key stays the protocol name.

description.description: What the tool does, shown to MCP clients in tools/list.

readOnlyHint.description: Hint to clients that the tool does not modify its environment.

destructiveHint.description: Hint that the tool may perform destructive updates.

idempotentHint.description: Hint that repeated calls with the same arguments have no additional effect.

openWorldHint.description: Hint that the tool interacts with external entities beyond the site.

annotations.description: Optional MCP behavior hints, passed to clients as declared; they are advisory and grant or restrict nothing.

inputSchema.description: Schema of the arguments object, in the bounded request.body.<METHOD>.schema JSON Schema 2020-12 profile (checked and compiled at activation); a call whose arguments fail it never reaches the handler.

outputSchema.description: Optional schema, in the same profile, of the object the handler returns; the result is then sent as structuredContent and a result that fails it is an error.

oneOf.description: Project-relative module path; its default export is the hook.

source.description: Project-relative path of the trusted hook module, resolved like a function route source and re-imported on each activation.

export.description: Named export to call (default: the module default export).

sandbox.description: Schema-valid but refused at activation when true: extension hooks run trusted, in-process, and are never sandboxed.

sandboxReason.description: Reviewer note recorded with a sandbox choice; it grants nothing.

handler.description: Called with the validated arguments and a context (granted env, request id, server and tool names); returns the result or throws McpToolError for an isError answer. Trusted project module ({source, export} or a bare path), run in-process like other extension hooks; sandbox: true is refused.

tools.description: Tools by protocol name (tools/list, tools/call); at least one.

uri.description: URI clients read the resource by (resources/read); unique within the server.

title.description: Human-readable display name (the MCP title field); the key stays the protocol name.

description.description: What the resource holds, shown to clients.

mimeType.description: MIME type advertised for the resource content.

oneOf.description: Project-relative module path; its default export is the hook.

source.description: Project-relative path of the trusted hook module, resolved like a function route source and re-imported on each activation.

export.description: Named export to call (default: the module default export).

sandbox.description: Schema-valid but refused at activation when true: extension hooks run trusted, in-process, and are never sandboxed.

sandboxReason.description: Reviewer note recorded with a sandbox choice; it grants nothing.

handler.description: Returns the resource content: a string, or {text or blob, mimeType}. Trusted project module ({source, export} or a bare path), run in-process like other extension hooks; sandbox: true is refused.

title.description: Human-readable display name (the MCP title field); the key stays the protocol name.

description.description: What the prompt produces, shown to clients.

name.description: Argument name; its value is a string.

description.description: What the argument means, shown to clients.

required.description: true: prompts/get without it is refused before the handler runs.

arguments.description: Declared string arguments of the prompt template.

oneOf.description: Project-relative module path; its default export is the hook.

source.description: Project-relative path of the trusted hook module, resolved like a function route source and re-imported on each activation.

export.description: Named export to call (default: the module default export).

sandbox.description: Schema-valid but refused at activation when true: extension hooks run trusted, in-process, and are never sandboxed.

sandboxReason.description: Reviewer note recorded with a sandbox choice; it grants nothing.

handler.description: Receives the validated string arguments and returns the prompt message content (prompts/get). Trusted project module ({source, export} or a bare path), run in-process like other extension hooks; sandbox: true is refused.

prompts.description: Optional prompt templates by name (prompts/list, prompts/get).

authoring.description: Declare a bounded MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool/resource/prompt server: named tools with a description, a request.body.<METHOD>.schema-shaped input (and optional output) schema, an optional title and optional behavior annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint), named URI-addressed resources, and named prompt templates (resources and prompts also take an optional title), each backed by a trusted project handler. The extension owns JSON-RPC 2.0 framing, protocol version negotiation, request-id handling, cursor pagination and initialize/ping/tools-*/resources-*/prompts-* dispatch; project YAML never carries JSON-RPC mechanics, a transport choice or provider settings.

surfaces.name: servers
surfaces.description: Declare one or more MCP servers, each with a mount, serverName, serverVersion, optional instructions and bounded tools/resources/prompts maps.

surfaces.name: tool handler
surfaces.description: Each tool declares a trusted project module/export handler (source, optional export), loaded and run the same way as other extension hooks: not sandboxed, receives the schema-validated arguments object and a context carrying the granted env of the mount route, the request id and the server/tool names. It returns the result value, or throws McpToolError (exported by @jimhoyd/urlcode-mcp) with a caller-facing message (and optional data returned as structuredContent when it conforms to the declared outputSchema) to answer isError: true; any other thrown error answers a fixed generic message.

surfaces.name: resource handler
surfaces.description: Each resource declares a trusted project module/export handler returning that resource’s content (a string, or {text|blob, mimeType}), served over resources/read.

surfaces.name: prompt handler
surfaces.description: Each prompt declares a trusted project module/export handler receiving the schema-validated string arguments and returning prompt message content, served over prompts/get.

surfaces.name: mount
surfaces.description: Mount each server at its declared path with POST (and HEAD); the protocol is stateless, so GET and DELETE are answered 405. The operator may enable streamed progress replies in host.mjs. Add `auth: true` when tool calls require a signed-in caller.

agent.description: Local, revision-pinned references for agents configuring the MCP extension.

references.name: MCP extension guide
references.description: Configuration and deployment guidance for project-defined MCP tools; ends with the generated field reference for every configuration key.
